### Vocabulary in scope

New at this step:
- contract (also: model boundary) — it is necessary that each contract declares at least 1 port (HCP L6 — Provenance.Contract: a declared model boundary with its members and ports)
- port — it is necessary that each port is a port of exactly one contract (HCP L6 — Provenance.Contract)
- member — it is necessary that each member is a member of exactly one contract (HCP L6 — Provenance.Contract)
- output port (also: result port) — it is obligatory that each output port is governed by at least 1 requirement (HCP L6 — NodeId.result, PortDir.output; #kind_requirement_clean fails on an ungoverned output)
- requirement — it is necessary that each requirement governs exactly one port (HCP L6 — Provenance.Requirement (statement, governs, port, scope, witness, absent, gate, referents, spotChecks))
- provable requirement — it is necessary that each provable requirement is discharged by exactly one proof (HCP L6 — RequirementKind.provable: discharged by a proof)
- empirical requirement — it is necessary that each empirical requirement is decided by exactly one gate (HCP L6 — RequirementKind.empirical: decided by a gate)
- proof — it is necessary that each proof discharges at least 1 provable requirement (HCP L6 — RequirementKind.provable)
- gate — it is necessary that each gate decides at least 1 empirical requirement (HCP L6 — RequirementKind.empirical)
- cleanliness gate — it is necessary that each cleanliness gate examines exactly one contract (HCP L6 — #kind_requirement_clean: the gate that fails on any ungoverned or unchecked output)
- scope — it is necessary that each scope is the scope of at least 1 requirement (HCP L6 — RequirementScope.sort, RequirementScope.objects: what a requirement quantifies over)
- referent — it is necessary that each referent is a referent of exactly one empirical requirement (HCP L6 — @[kindReferent]: an empirical referent)
- counterexample (also: refuting witness) — it is necessary that each counterexample refutes exactly one requirement (HCP L6 — @[kindCounterexample]: a refuting witness)
- *contract* declares *port* — verb
- *port* is a port of *contract* — verb
- *member* is a member of *contract* — verb
- *requirement* governs *port* — verb
- *port* is governed by *requirement* — verb
- *proof* discharges *provable requirement* — verb
- *provable requirement* is discharged by *proof* — verb
- *gate* decides *empirical requirement* — verb
- *empirical requirement* is decided by *gate* — verb
- *cleanliness gate* examines *contract* — verb
- *requirement* quantifies over *scope* — verb
- *scope* is the scope of *requirement* — verb
- *referent* is a referent of *empirical requirement* — verb
- *counterexample* refutes *requirement* — verb
